items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Yank and Bob Haggard had gone to Decca Records, and approached Milt Galber... Milt was well known as a musician's friend... Yank came down to see me at work and said we were going to record, that they had signed us up for a series of albums

ctx.x: But he was one of the mainstays of that Lawson-Haggard band, for sure.

That night over at Lou Stein's house, we made a demo, and I went back to my job, and heard nothing -- I went for a few weeks, but we had a nice night, we had a lovely time. We had a very good social night, too. But we were recording five or six songs, and apparently in the meantime, Yank and Bob Haggard had gone to Decca Records, and approached Milt Galber. Now Milt was well known as a musician's friend and so forth -- he had the original Commodore Record Company, which was, did nothing but jazz research for…

To sum it up better, that was the begining of a beautiful thing --' recording wise and friendship wise, and a series of albums, running between 20 and 30. We made in the middle twenties, amoung of albums.
